scope: Bibliography verification, anonymous artifact-citation mapping, novelty bound, and nonidentifying companion-paper overlap only. The recovered manuscript is not rewritten here; NS-022 integrates verified_references.bib and applies the label replacements.

source_versions.dissertation_catalog: EECS HTML title Program Synthesis By Sketching for UCB/EECS-2008-176, retrieved 2026-09-11; EECS-2008-164 rejected as a different report

criteria.criterion: Every citation resolves to a primary bibliographic source or accessible anonymous artifact and supports the adjacent statement.
criteria.explanation: All twelve reconstructed entries resolve to a Crossref DOI or the verified EECS dissertation catalog page. Each in-text use of [1]–[12] matches the cited work's actual contribution. Internal workstream labels are mapped to anonymous supplement identifiers or scientific descriptions rather than left as bibliography entries.

criteria.criterion: No unresolvable internal shorthand or identifying repository link remains in the submission.
criteria.explanation: This task's submission-facing outputs contain no GitHub, Overleaf, username, or author-repository URL. Every D/A/N/K/P/W token, Table 13 program name, PCTDD/M1–M3 stage, and B1 author-local worktree is resolved to an anonymous supplement id, a scientific description, or explicit removal. Manuscript application of those replacements is NS-022; these outputs do not leave unresolved shorthand in the verified bibliography or citation map.

criteria.criterion: Claims of novelty are bounded by the literature and the experiment, without invented first-of-kind claims.
criteria.explanation: The audit retains the draft's own bound: the twelve works are foundations or baselines, not newly invented algorithms; the intended contribution is the supervision/evidence composition at the agent boundary; the paper does not claim to be the first neurosymbolic agent or that combination automatically improves performance. No first-of-kind or unrun-benchmark claim is added.

criteria.criterion: Shared data/code/evaluation across the three submissions is disclosed appropriately and not double-counted as independent replication.
criteria.explanation: The overlap audit names the three distinct research questions, the two shared bibliographic works (translation validation and Thor), the shared kernel/translation/native-proof/storage surfaces, and the counting rules that forbid treating one inspection, one unavailable prover, or Table 5 preliminary arithmetic as three independent results. Companion evaluations are different protocols and oracles.
